name: Korvel Ube-Tamarind Dark
description: A small-batch dark soda from a second-generation family bottler, Korvel blends real ube extract with tamarind concentrate in a cola-adjacent dark base. One of the few family-owned soda operations still running in M88's Tier 2 belt.
flavor_profile: Deep, earthy ube sweetness with purple-vanilla character; tamarind's sour-sweet complexity winds through the middle; the dark cola base adds roasted bitterness; long, complex finish that evolves over seconds
cultural_context: Korvel & Sons is the kind of brand that loyal customers are evangelical about — a small but intensely devoted following; the real ube extract is a genuine point of difference at this price point; the family's continued independence from corponation buyout is a minor legend in the M88 food scene.
story_hooks: Mirela Korvel, the 70-year-old matriarch who controls the ube sourcing contracts, has received a death threat — someone wants the family to sell, and they're escalating.
Korvel's latest batch has an unusual secondary fermentation happening in sealed bottles — it's not dangerous, but it's creating a mild euphoric effect, and word is spreading fast on the street.
A Tier 4 corponation food executive has been secretly purchasing Korvel in bulk through shell buyers — someone wants to reverse-engineer the formula before making a final buyout offer.
